curation.lead:
The Kuhn Foundation (EIN 33-0783933) is a 501(c)(3) private operating foundation established in 1999 by Robert Lawrence Kuhn to produce Closer To Truth, a long-running PBS science series. Registered at 723 Euclid St, Unit B, Santa Monica, CA 90402, the foundation held $9–12 million in assets at Morgan Stanley SmithBarney and was run as a family enterprise — Kuhn as president (25 hrs/week), with his wife Dora as vice president, sons Aaron and Adam as VP and CFO, and daughter Daniella as secretary, all at zero compensation. Its sole program was CTT television production. Between August 2017 and June 2018, the foundation received $650,000 from Gratitude America Ltd, Jeffrey Epstein’s USVI-registered private foundation funded primarily by Leon Black’s $10 million donation.

The Epstein money entered a dedicated sub-account Kuhn created specifically for the purpose: “Kuhn Foundation CTT JE – Radical Breakthroughs,” where “JE” stood for Jeffrey Epstein. The funds supported a 13-episode PBS season called Radical Breakthroughs, covering topics from mathematical truth to consciousness. Epstein was not a passive donor — he actively shaped episode content, directed which topics to cut, and proposed new ones. The relationship went well beyond science patronage: Kuhn deliberately kept Epstein’s sponsorship secret from PBS, assessed which scientists were “safe” for Epstein to meet, and served simultaneously as a geopolitical intelligence channel — providing Epstein real-time analysis of Chinese and Middle Eastern leadership dynamics drawn from Kuhn’s extraordinary access as a 30-year advisor to the Chinese government and host on CGTN state television.

The Kuhn Foundation thus operated at the intersection of two distinct Epstein functions: scientific reputation-laundering through legitimate PBS programming, and geopolitical information brokerage through Kuhn’s dual role as media host and advisor to Chinese leadership. The foundation’s legitimate scale ($9–12M in assets, two decades of CTT production) gave the Epstein funding the appearance of ordinary philanthropic support for science media, while the dedicated “JE” sub-account, the secrecy protocols, and the temporal coincidence of the first wire with a Belt and Road discussion suggest a more transactional arrangement. At least 20 documented meetings occurred between Epstein and Kuhn from October 2016 through June 2019 — the last just 23 days before Epstein’s arrest.

sections.title: Corporate Identity and Structure
sections.content:
The Kuhn Foundation is a California-based 501(c)(3) private operating foundation (EIN 33-0783933) with an IRS ruling date of April 29, 1999. It is classified under NTEE code A99 (Arts, Culture & Humanities) and registered at 723 Euclid St, Unit B, Santa Monica, CA 90402. A second address — 357 Waverly Dr, Pasadena, CA 91105 — appears in Gratitude America correspondence and may be Robert Lawrence Kuhn’s personal residence used for grant paperwork.

As a private operating foundation, the Kuhn Foundation makes zero outgoing grants. It operates programs directly — specifically, the production of Closer To Truth (CTT), a PBS television series exploring science, philosophy, and consciousness that has aired since 2000. This structure is important: the foundation’s annual 990-PF filings consistently show a single program activity (CTT production) and $0 officer compensation. End-of-year 2018 assets totaled $12,075,165, held primarily at Morgan Stanley SmithBarney, with a small $66,895 position in Sealantis Ltd, an Israeli biotech company. The foundation’s accountant is William H. Hranchak of Temo Arjani LLP, Pasadena. The family governance structure — five Kuhn family members filling all officer positions at zero compensation — means the foundation exists essentially as a personal production vehicle for Robert Kuhn’s television work.

sections.title: Epstein Financial Flows
sections.content:
The financial relationship began with a February 15, 2017 exchange in which Epstein asked Kuhn: “is it a charity that received the funding?” Kuhn responded by sending the IRS tax-exempt determination letter, establishing the Kuhn Foundation as the fiscal conduit months before any money moved. On July 31, 2017, Epstein replied to a Kuhn email about China’s “Belt and Road” initiative with: “details of where to wire money?” The next day, August 1, 2017, Kuhn sent formal wiring instructions for a newly created sub-account: “Kuhn Foundation CTT JE – Radical Breakthroughs,” described as “dedicated to our project, to facilitate monitoring use of funds.” The first wire — $150,000 from Gratitude America — landed that same day.

The second tranche came on June 14, 2018, when Epstein wrote to his financial manager Richard Kahn: “robert kuhn we need to send 600k from foundation. remind me torow.” Kahn confirmed the prior $150K had been sent on 8/1/2017 and asked about paperwork, referencing Darren Indyke. By June 15, Epstein revised the amount downward: “send 500k today.” Total confirmed Gratitude America disbursements: $650,000 ($150K + $500K). The 2018 IRS 990 XML for Gratitude America (EIN 66-0789697) confirms the $500,000 grant on Schedule I.

The impact on the foundation’s finances was substantial. In 2018, the Kuhn Foundation reported $1,216,825 in contributions (line 1) — a dramatic spike compared to normal years when contributions were negligible and revenue came primarily from investment returns ($233K–$793K annually in 2011–2013). The $500K Gratitude America grant represented 41% of total 2018 contributions. The foundation spent $1,339,333 on CTT production that year, with its only external grant being $17,500 to KOCE-TV Foundation, a PBS station in Los Angeles. A March 2019 email from Kuhn revealed that JEVIF (Jeffrey Epstein VI Foundation) was the true underwriting source, with Kuhn writing about optimizing “for JEVI Foundation as well as CTT.” Epstein separately confirmed to Gretchen Buhlig: “the formal name is jevi the name on the check was enhanced foundation.”

sections.title: Secrecy Protocols and Reputational Management
sections.content:
A critical March 27–28, 2019 email thread reveals the deliberate secrecy strategy Kuhn maintained around Epstein’s sponsorship of CTT Radical Breakthroughs. Kuhn wrote to Epstein: “My original thinking was to keep your/JEVIF underwriting/sponsor relatively secret until the shows are broadcast — then, after all see our CTT Breakthroughs full season of 13 episodes… we will be in a strong position to go public and be proud.” He explicitly warned: “I worry that someone might tell their girlfriend or cousin, who could try to make a problem with PBS.”

Kuhn’s risk management extended to curating which scientists Epstein could safely meet. He advised Epstein to meet mathematician Gregory Chaitin one-on-one but specifically excluded Danny Chamovitz because “his new position as president of Ben Gurion University might make him nervous.” This was not paranoia but operational security: Kuhn understood that a university president associating with a convicted sex offender would create institutional blowback that could unravel the entire production. The pattern shows Kuhn functioning as a reputational gatekeeper — managing the boundary between Epstein’s intellectual aspirations and the public exposure that could destroy them.

Epstein, for his part, was not merely writing checks. He actively shaped the series content, directing Kuhn to “cut 11 12 and 13. add, antibiotics and their cognitive impacts.” He rejected topics he found unsatisfying (“did not like multi verse and sensience. seems more blahblah”) and proposed his own (“do we dream all day, can we use music as an insight into the brain that produced it, mathematics relies on truth, biology relies on deception”). This level of editorial involvement went well beyond typical philanthropy. The dedicated “JE” sub-account, the secrecy from PBS, and Epstein’s content direction together indicate a relationship more accurately described as production partnership with hidden ownership than charitable grant-making.

sections.title: The China Intelligence Channel
sections.content:
Robert Lawrence Kuhn is one of the most connected Americans to Chinese leadership. According to his biography in the Epstein files (HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_023666), Kuhn has advised the Chinese government for over 30 years, authored the official biography of President Jiang Zemin (China’s best-selling book in 2005), spoke at the launch of Xi Jinping’s Governance of China, hosts Closer to China with R.L. Kuhn on CGTN (Chinese state television), and was interviewed 24 times on CNN and BBC during the 19th CPC Congress alone. In December 2018, Xi Jinping awarded Kuhn the China Reform Friendship Medal — one of ten given to foreign nationals.

This geopolitical access ran in parallel with the science-media relationship. Kuhn regularly sent Epstein analysis of Chinese politics, Belt and Road strategy, Trump-era trade tensions, Xi’s power consolidation, and North Korea developments. The temporal coincidence of the first $150K payment with a Belt and Road email exchange is suggestive: Epstein’s “details of where to wire money?” came as a direct reply to Kuhn’s China briefing. On November 9, 2016, Kuhn emailed Epstein from Beijing about the Trump election: “You are a prophet… I forgot to congratulate you on winning your l000000ng-odds bet on Trump with Woody. Everyone I know, including me, would have bet against you. Quite extraordinary.”

This dual-track relationship — science media and geopolitical intelligence — made Kuhn uniquely valuable in Epstein’s network. The Kuhn Foundation funded the science track, but the China track ran through the same personal relationship. Kuhn’s regular CGTN appearances and absence of FARA registration, combined with the China Reform Friendship Medal from Xi and the interleaving of China analysis with PBS funding discussions, raise questions about the full scope of information flowing through this channel. Epstein’s October 4, 2016 schedule placed Kuhn alongside Leon Black, Vitaly Churkin (Russian UN Ambassador who died months later), and Peter Thiel — a constellation of financial, diplomatic, and intelligence connections meeting the same person on the same day.

sections.title: Scientist Brokerage Network
sections.content:
Beyond producing television, the Kuhn Foundation’s Radical Breakthroughs series served as a vehicle through which Kuhn brokered connections between Epstein and world-class scientists. The production team — Kuhn as host/writer and Peter Getzels as producer/director — assembled a roster of interviewees that overlapped substantially with Epstein’s existing science network. Key scientists included Misha Gromov (mathematician, added to the series in December 2017), Giulio Tononi (consciousness researcher, Integrated Information Theory), Gregory Chaitin (algorithmic information theory), Paul Davies (physicist), V.S. Ramachandran (neuroscientist), Danny Chamovitz (plant biology, president of Ben Gurion University), and Martin Nowak of Harvard’s Program for Evolutionary Dynamics — Epstein’s longest-running academic affiliation.

Several of these scientists were independently connected to Epstein before appearing on the series. Gromov and Nowak in particular had pre-existing Epstein relationships. The April 6, 2019 meeting at Epstein’s residence included Kuhn, Chaitin (with wife and infant), and producer Getzels. In May–June 2019, Kuhn conducted filming interviews in Boston, including with Nowak, then returned to New York — just weeks before Epstein’s July 6 arrest. Epstein’s calendar shows Kuhn meetings frequently scheduled alongside other high-value contacts: the December 1, 2018 entry reads “10:00am Appt w/Misha Gromov, 12:00pm Appt w/Robert Kuhn, 12:30pm Appt w/Vincenzo Lozze, 2:00pm Go See Kathy Ruemmler’s NEW Apartment, 5:00pm Appt w/Richard Axel.” At least 20 documented meetings between Epstein and Kuhn occurred from October 2016 through June 2019, demonstrating sustained, high-frequency engagement rather than occasional philanthropic check-ins.
